heading: Energy Storage Intelligence
subheading: Grid-scale batteries, the storage software layer & next-gen chemistry
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Storage names face Chinese competition and policy risk. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.sub: US BATTERY STORAGE — EIA STILL SEES NEARLY 65 GW BY YEAR-END
kpis.label: EIA's mid-2026 count has operating capacity near 52 GW after 8.3 GW came online in H1, with 64.9 GW still targeted by year-end as developers plan a record 24 GW of utility-scale additions in 2026 — up from 15 GW in 2025 — with another 89 GW pipelined for 2027

kpis.sub: FLUENCE SLASHES FY26 GUIDANCE, DISCLOSES SEC PROBE
kpis.label: Fluence cut FY26 revenue guidance to ~$2.4B (from ~$3.0B) and adjusted EBITDA to a ~$200M loss (from a ~$10M loss) on Sept 16, citing Houston contract-manufacturing delays; shares fell 15.4% to $7.66 the next day and the company disclosed an SEC investigation into revenue recognition and internal controls

kpis.sub: GE VERNOVA BACKLOG STEADY, CEO SEES $200B EARLY 2027
kpis.label: Backlog held at $176B through Q2 (+37% YoY); CEO Scott Strazik said Sept 16 that Q3 order strength gives him confidence backlog could cross $200B very early in 2027 — even as shares, near $925 on Sept 17, are down more than 14% over the past month on broader sector rotation

kpis.sub: EOS ENERGY: DOE LOAN ADVANCE FUNDS THORN HILL RAMP
kpis.label: Eos received an $87M advance on its DOE loan for the Thorn Hill plant's second production line (toward 2GWh, then 4GWh), while shares climbed from $3.04 to $4.08 over two weeks as the formalized 10MW/100MWh Z3 deal with Google/MN8 in West Virginia kept sentiment constructive; Roth Capital lifted its target to $4.50 (Neutral)

bear_case.title: China dominates cells — and domestic rivalry is compressing terms further
bear_case.description: CATL still holds the global No.1 BESS shipment position for H1 2026 (storage now 19.23% of its revenue), and just locked in a 10-year, up-to-200GWh supply deal with Beijing HyperStrong running through 2028 — deepening its grip on the value chain. BYD and Sungrow's earlier win of the Masdar deal already showed domestic rivalry compresses terms on its own; combined, CATL and BYD now account for 62.43% of battery installations, the highest concentration in recent months.

bear_case.title: Tariffs keep rising, and FEOC/FERC rules add layers of cost and complexity
bear_case.description: Section 301 duties on Chinese-origin ESS batteries jumped from 40.9% in 2025 to 58.4% in 2026, and FEOC content thresholds (55% domestic in 2026, rising to 75% after 2029) still risk disqualifying projects from the ITC. Layered on top, the FERC-directed PJM co-location rule rewrite remains mid-implementation in 2026 — transmission cost allocation under the new framework directly affects grid-services revenue for data-center-adjacent storage names like NRGV and Cummins' customers.

bear_case.title: Fluence's crisis is now weighing on how the market reads the whole hardware/software stack
bear_case.description: Fluence cut FY26 revenue guidance by $600M and swung its EBITDA outlook from a $10M loss to a $200M loss, disclosed an SEC investigation into revenue recognition and internal controls, and saw shares fall 15.4% in a single session — on top of three sell-side downgrades already in place from early September. At least five law firms have since opened shareholder investigations. Stem's slide to a fresh 52-week low despite positive adjusted EBITDA suggests the market is now discounting execution risk across the software/optimization layer too, not just Fluence's hardware integration.

bear_case.title: Solid-state timelines keep slipping while China's catches up
bear_case.description: QuantumScape shares are down roughly 51% YTD with no fresh catalysts this month, and recent CTO share sales add a mildly negative signal; the PowerCo licensing deal still targets only a 2027 commercial launch with no production license or revenue yet. CATL and BYD are both still publicly targeting 2027 solid-state trial production, meaning the assumed Western first-mover advantage in solid-state keeps eroding rather than firming up.

catalysts.title: DIMAAG-AI and Toshiba partner on AI data-center storage using lithium-titanate cells
catalysts.description: The collaboration pairs Toshiba's SCiB lithium-titanate technology with DIMAAG's immersion-cooled architecture, targeting continuous 10C charge/discharge and 10+ year service life for load smoothing and backup power at AI data centers.

Overlaps your Nuclear sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Eos Energy
positions.note: Raised a point, funded by trimming NRGV below: the Google/MN8 deal firmed up to a specific 10MW/100MWh contract and an $87M DOE loan advance is now funding the Thorn Hill second line — real de-risking events, not just sentiment, even though storage revenue on this deal still doesn't start until 2028–2030 and the securities-law investigations remain open.

positions.name: QuantumScape

positions.name: Energy Vault Holdings

positions.name: Fluence Energy
positions.note: Stays avoid, and the case just got stronger: a $600M FY26 revenue cut, an EBITDA swing from a $10M loss to a $200M loss, a disclosed SEC investigation into revenue recognition and internal controls, a 15.4% one-day share drop, and at least five law-firm shareholder investigations — this is no longer a margin story, it's a controls-and-credibility story.

positions.name: Enphase
positions.note: Shares fell 3.8% on Sept 18 alongside the broader solar complex as a Fed rate hike pressured residential financing demand — a macro move, not company-specific, and the Hold consensus ($45 average target) is unchanged, so the thesis stays exactly where it was: fine business, wrong price until the policy overhang clears.

positions.name: Stem Inc
positions.note: Trading just above its 52-week low even after a fifth straight quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA — the market keeps pricing top-line softness harder than the cost discipline offsets, and nothing this week changed that calculus; next earnings Oct 29 is the next real test.
